headings.text: What actually matters in a room air cooler

cta.headline: Match the cooler to your climate
cta.sub: A desert cooler in Mumbai is a damp disappointment. A personal cooler in Jaipur is barely enough.

faq.q: Do air coolers work in humid cities like Mumbai or Kolkata?
faq.a: Standard evaporative coolers add moisture to the air and work poorly above 60 percent relative humidity. In humid coastal cities, look for a cooler with a larger blower, ice compartment, or hybrid coolers that combine evaporative and fan modes.

faq.q: What size cooler do I need for my room?
faq.a: Personal coolers with 10 to 20 L tanks suit rooms up to 150 sq ft. Room coolers with 25 to 40 L tanks handle 150 to 300 sq ft. Desert coolers with 50 L or larger tanks cover 300 to 600 sq ft and need cross-ventilation.

faq.q: Plastic or metal body -- which is better?
faq.a: Plastic-bodied coolers are lighter, rust-free and cheaper. Metal-bodied coolers are more durable, easier to repair and last longer in dry climates. Pick plastic for coastal cities (salt air) and metal for dry inland cities.

faq.q: How much electricity does an air cooler use?
faq.a: A typical room cooler with a 100 to 200 W blower uses 0.1 to 0.2 units per hour. Running 8 hours at night costs roughly Rs 8 to Rs 16 on most Indian tariffs. A 1.5 ton AC uses 10 times more electricity for the same duration.
Most room coolers are plug-and-play. Position near a window for cross-ventilation, fill the tank, plug in, and run. Desert coolers may need a fixed water connection and an exhaust opening.
